forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 21%. June 2026 discourse remains noisy but the resolution bar is unmet: Nvidia's Huang has said 'we've achieved AGI' and Altman has used loose AGI language, but there is no clean credible-lab declaration of AGI, and rigorous benchmarks (ARC-AGI-2 at ~4% vs ~100% human) plus Stanford-expert scepticism argue against a formal 'AGI achieved' event before 2030.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: near-term insider predictions of a transformative technology arriving inside a fixed ~3.5-year window, where insiders carry strong optimism incentives. Such forecasts historically resolve YES well under half the time; base ~15-20%.

factors_up.factor: Lab leadership timelines (Amodei 2027, Hassabis ~50% by 2030) sit partly inside the window
Loose 'AGI' framing already in circulation (Huang, Altman) could harden into a declaration

factors_down.factor: Resolution bar (clean credible declaration or 3+ researchers) remains unmet and definitionally contested
Hard benchmarks (ARC-AGI-2 ~4%) and expert scepticism show persistent generality shortfalls

key_uncertainties: Whether any major lab will formally use the term 'AGI' in a declaration rather than avoiding it
Whether 3+ leading researchers would publicly converge on 'AGI achieved'
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible lab announces AGI or 3+ leading researchers state it is achieved
Revise DOWN if frontier progress visibly plateaus or labs explicitly disavow near-term AGI

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 26%. Reporting continues to confirm McKinsey's ~10% (3,000-4,000 role) cuts — its largest since 2008 — with Bain, BCG, Deloitte, KPMG and Accenture also trimming and AI compressing research/analysis hours. But a ≥33% decline in revenue or employment by 2030, primarily attributed to AI by 2+ credible analyses, remains a far higher bar than the ~10% structural cuts seen so far.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: established professional-services sectors losing a third or more of value/employment within ~6 years due to a single technology. Rare; base ~10-15%.

factors_up.factor: Largest consulting cuts since 2008, explicitly AI-linked, now industry-wide (McKinsey, Bain, BCG, Deloitte, KPMG, Accenture)
AI-native boutiques undercutting on price plus soft discretionary spend compounding the pressure

factors_down.factor: Cuts so far ~10%, an order of magnitude short of the 33% threshold
Attribution problem: separating AI from cyclical demand and proving 'primarily AI' is hard

key_uncertainties: Whether AI substitution accelerates non-linearly or plateaus after early efficiency gains
Whether credible analyses will attribute any decline primarily to AI rather than the cycle
update_triggers: Revise UP if multiple top firms report double-digit revenue declines explicitly tied to AI
Revise DOWN if headcount/revenue stabilises or firms redeploy staff into AI-advisory growth

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 5%. June 2026 polling averages put Reform UK well ahead (~27%) with Labour (~19%) statistically tied with the Conservatives (~19%) and the Greens rising. Labour trails the leader by ~8 points roughly mid-parliament. A recovery to largest-party status is possible before the late-2029 deadline but currently a long shot.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: governing parties ~8 points behind a clear poll leader at mid-parliament going on to win most seats. Uncommon but not unheard-of; base ~10-15%, tempered here by a fragmented multi-party field.

factors_up.factor: Up to ~3.5 years for recovery; incumbency and electoral machinery
Fragmented opposition (Reform, Con, Green, LD) could let Labour win most seats on a low vote share via FPTP

factors_down.factor: Reform's sustained, sizeable lead since mid-2025
Labour squeezed on multiple flanks, including Greens among younger voters

key_uncertainties: How FPTP converts a fragmented four/five-party vote into seats
Whether Reform's lead is durable or a mid-term protest spike
update_triggers: Revise UP if Labour recovers a polling lead or Reform's support collapses
Revise DOWN if Reform consolidates a structural lead into the election

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 81%. The ~9-year window comfortably contains most credible lab and researcher AGI timelines (Amodei, Hassabis ~50% by 2030, Altman within the decade). Over this horizon either capabilities reach a broadly accepted AGI threshold or definitional convergence makes a declaration likely; the main risk is an unexpected capability plateau.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: expert-forecast transformative technologies materialising within a ~9-year window when sustained capital and capability momentum is already visible. Resolves YES more often than not; base ~60-70%.

factors_up.factor: Most insider timelines fall well inside the window
Sustained scaling, capital and agentic-capability progress

factors_down.factor: Definitional contestation could delay any agreed 'AGI achieved' declaration
Possible capability plateau or scaling/compute limits before 2035

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling and algorithmic progress continue or hit diminishing returns
Whether the field converges on a declarable AGI definition
update_triggers: Revise UP if frontier systems clear recognised generality benchmarks
Revise DOWN if progress stalls or a long AI winter sets in

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 8%. PLA blockade rehearsals continue (Strait Thunder 2025A, Justice Mission 2025, including 'cutting off power' drills and LNG-terminal targeting), and Taiwan is hardening LNG reserves and escort plans. But analysts still centre 2027 as the capability milestone, and there is no kinetic move; a >72hr blockade or assault before 2030 remains low-probability.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: major-power initiation of a blockade/invasion against a defended territory within a fixed ~3.5-year window amid deterrence. Rare; base ~5-10%.

factors_up.factor: Escalating, increasingly realistic PLA blockade rehearsals and target-marking
2027 frequently cited as a PLA capability milestone, partly inside the window

factors_down.factor: No kinetic action; drills remain coercive signalling short of war
US/allied deterrence and severe economic costs to Beijing

key_uncertainties: Whether Beijing converts rehearsal capability into actual initiation
How cross-strait politics and US posture evolve through 2027-2029
update_triggers: Revise UP on mobilisation indicators, declared quarantine, or a major escalation
Revise DOWN on cross-strait de-escalation or credible deterrence reinforcement

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged down 1pp to 4%. ONS data (released 17 June) shows CPI at 2.8% in the 12 months to May 2026, unchanged from April and above the 2% target, with transport inflation accelerating to 6.8%. With only six monthly prints left before 2027 and headline stuck near 2.8%, a sub-2.0% month looks very unlikely.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: headline CPI falling >0.8pp below an entrenched ~2.8% level within six months absent a demand shock. Uncommon; base ~5-10%.

factors_up.factor: Food inflation decelerating sharply (2.2%, lowest since Dec 2024)
Possible energy/base-effect downside surprise in H2 2026

factors_down.factor: Headline stuck at 2.8% with transport inflation surging to 6.8%
Sticky services inflation and only six prints remaining

key_uncertainties: Energy and fuel price path into late 2026
update_triggers: Revise UP if a sharp energy decline or demand shock drags CPI toward 2%
Revise DOWN if inflation re-accelerates or holds near 3%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 1pp to 84%. With a 31 July 2026 release, the film has posted the best US single-day presales in five years (4th-largest of all time) and tracks toward a ~$200M opening with $1B+ widely expected. Five months of run before year-end gives ample room to clear $1.5B, though that bar sits well above the ~$1B base case and only one solo Spider-Man film has ever reached it.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: tentpole Spider-Man/MCU sequels crossing $1.5B worldwide. Among solo Spider-Man films only No Way Home cleared it; base for a marquee, hype-leading entry ~50-65%, lifted by exceptional presales.

factors_up.factor: Long ~5-month runway to year-end and prime summer slot

factors_down.factor: $1.5B is far above the ~$1B central projection; only one solo Spidey film hit it
Reviews/word-of-mouth or China performance could cap the multiplier

key_uncertainties: Final reception and legs after opening weekend
update_triggers: Revise UP on a record opening and strong holds
Revise DOWN on a soft opening or weak word-of-mouth

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 98%. May/June 2026 reporting puts Anthropic at ~$30B (some estimates up to ~$47B) and OpenAI at a ~$33B run rate, so the combined figure is already at or above $70B on most measures, with steep growth into Q4. The main residual risk is accounting disputes over how 'credible' ARR is defined and reported for Q4 2026.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: hypergrowth AI leaders sustaining a combined run-rate already near a threshold through two more quarters. Resolves YES very often; base ~85-90%.

factors_up.factor: Combined run-rate already ~$63-80B and growing fast
Strong enterprise demand and continued capital inflows

factors_down.factor: Accounting disputes (e.g. gross-revenue overstatement claims) could muddy 'credible' Q4 figures
Tail risk of a sharp demand/funding shock before year-end

key_uncertainties: Which ARR figures the resolving sources treat as credible
Whether reporting cadence yields clean Q4 2026 numbers for both
update_triggers: Revise UP if both firms confirm rising ARR with consistent methodology
Revise DOWN if a major reporting/accounting dispute or demand shock emerges

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: No change at 39%. The OBR's March 2026 outlook puts potential output growth around 1.5% in 2029 with TFP revised down (to ~0.8%) and only a modest AI uplift (~0.2pp by the horizon); per-person growth is ~1.1%. With the central path sitting essentially on the 1.5% threshold and ageing-population/productivity headwinds into the 2030s, a full-decade average above 1.5% is roughly a sub-coin-flip.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: advanced-economy decade-average real GDP growth exceeding a threshold set right at the central potential-growth estimate. Roughly even odds, tilted down by recent downgrades; base ~40-45%.

factors_up.factor: AI/productivity upside could exceed the OBR's cautious assumptions
Population growth and investment could lift headline GDP above per-capita trends

factors_down.factor: OBR TFP downgrade and central potential growth only ~1.5%
Ageing demographics and persistent productivity weakness into the 2030s

key_uncertainties: Whether AI delivers a material productivity boost in the 2030s
update_triggers: Revise UP on evidence of a sustained productivity acceleration
Revise DOWN on further potential-growth downgrades or weak 2030s starts
